patterns_discovered.description: Applied git branch -d first (8 branches deleted), then git branch -D for remaining branches requiring force delete (5 branches)
patterns_discovered.evidence: Subtask 3.3 deleted 8 branches safely, then force-deleted 5 branches where HEAD differed from dev

patterns_discovered.description: Verified that force-deleted branches had no commits not in dev before executing deletion
patterns_discovered.evidence: All 5 force-deleted branches were confirmed to have all work merged into dev

gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Force Delete vs Safe Delete Decision
gotchas_discovered.description: 5 branches required force delete (-D flag) instead of safe delete (-d) because HEAD was different from dev, despite all work being merged
gotchas_discovered.impact: Initial safe deletes succeeded for 8 branches, but remaining 5 required alternative approach
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Verified that all commits existed in dev before proceeding with force delete

gotchas_discovered.description: Branch merge status not immediately obvious from branch listing; required commit comparison to verify true merge status
gotchas_discovered.impact: Unable to delete all 13 branches with single strategy; required two-phase deletion
gotchas_discovered.lesson: Git branch tracking can lag actual commit state; verify with git log before destructive operations

gotchas_discovered.description: Current worktree branch (auto-claude/022) cannot be deleted while the worktree is active
gotchas_discovered.impact: Must keep branch 022 as long as working in that worktree
gotchas_discovered.lesson: Active worktree branches are protected and should not be included in batch deletion operations

gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Implicit Dependencies Between Branches and Worktrees
gotchas_discovered.description: Deleting auto-claude/014 branch also required removing its associated worktree in previous subtask
gotchas_discovered.impact: Branch deletion and worktree cleanup must be coordinated
gotchas_discovered.lesson: Track relationships between branches and worktrees to avoid broken references
